name: PS5 WebKit to IPv6 pktopts UAF (CVE-2020-7457)

root_cause.summary: The IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS setsockopt handler lacks synchronization, so concurrent calls race on ip6_pktopts and can modify a packet-options object after it has been freed (CVE-2020-7457, FreeBSD-SA-20:20). On PS5 the WebKit stage first obtains arbitrary userland read/write, then triggers the race and reclaims the freed ip6_pktopts with ip6_rthdr sprays; the pktopts/rthdr overlap yields kernel read/write. XOM and the hypervisor prevent kernel code execution, so the public chain stops at read/write and data patches.
root_cause.primitive: race-condition use-after-free of ip6_pktopts (0x100 slab) reclaimed with ip6_rthdr sprays
root_cause.trigger: concurrent setsockopt(IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS) calls from the WebKit process
root_cause.consequence: kernel arbitrary read/write; no kernel code execution on PS5 because kernel .text is XOM and the hypervisor enforces write protection

discovery_approach.summary: The IPv6 bug is FreeBSD CVE-2020-7457, credited to syzkaller and Andy Nguyen and fixed upstream in 2020. TheFlow adapted it to the PlayStation kernel; ChendoChap and Znullptr built the PS5 WebKit userland stage for 4.03 (CSSFontFaceSet, with a Web Worker stack pivot to bypass clang CFI), and Cryptogenic packaged the IPv6 kernel exploit for 3.00-4.51. The browser is reached through the PS5 User Manual: DNS-redirect manuals.playstation.net to a local HTTPS server and accept the untrusted certificate.
signals: the IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS set handler missing synchronization
ip6_pktopts freed while a racing setsockopt still references it
the PS5 User Manual / modal browser as the WebKit host
clang CFI is forward-edge only and there is no shadow stack, so a Web Worker return address is a viable pivot

firmware.fixed_in: unknown on PS5; FreeBSD fixed CVE-2020-7457 upstream in 2020 (SA-20:20)
differences: PS5 keeps clang CFI (forward-edge only) and XOM; the WebKit stage pivots through a Web Worker return address instead of the PS4 vtable-smash strategy (ChendoChap).
kernel .text is XOM and the hypervisor enforces write protection, so the IPv6 UAF yields kernel read/write but not code execution or kernel patches (Cryptogenic PS5-IPV6-Kernel-Exploit).

patch_evidence.what: FreeBSD-SA-20:20 names the missing synchronization in the IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS set handler, assigns CVE-2020-7457 and gives the corrected revisions; the PS5 wiki records the 3.00-4.51 affected range
patch_evidence.limits: no PS5-specific patch version or binary diff is public; the FreeBSD fix is upstream, not a Sony advisory

sources.supports: CVE-2020-7457: the IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS set handler was missing synchronization, racing accesses could modify freed memory, impact is memory corruption/privilege escalation, corrected revisions
PS5 4.03 browser was vulnerable to the CSSFontFaceSet WebKit bug; clang CFI blocks PS4-style vtable smashing; Web Worker stack leak and stack pivot at stack+0x7FB88; userland-only scope
PS5 3.00-4.51 IPv6 UAF exploit; 5 stages (ip6_pktopts UAF, ip6_rthdr spray, kqueue/pktopts leak, IPV6_RTHDR R/W, cleanup/patch); XOM/HV prevent kernel code execution; DNS-redirect User Manual entry
IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS UAF at PS5 3.00-4.51, and the CSSFontFaceSet WebKit exploit range 3.00-4.51
the WebKit (CSSFontFaceSet/loadInSameDocument) plus IPv6 UAF chains for PS5 1.00-5.50 and 3.00-4.51

gaps: No PS5-specific patch version is public; the wiki records only the affected range 3.00-4.51.
The WebKit bug used for the PS5 userland stage is described as CSSFontFaceSet in the wiki, but ChendoChap's README does not name the CVE; the exact bug identity is a gap.
The chain stops at kernel read/write because of XOM/HV, so there is no public PS5 kernel code execution from this path.
The FreeBSD advisory is the upstream bug; the PS5 kernel's exact backport state and fix version are not documented in the fetched sources.

entry_chain.runtime_only: the DNS/HTTPS setup and the untrusted-certificate acceptance
